requirements.requirement: On node1, persistently disable acceptance of IPv4 ICMP redirects and source-routed packets.
requirements.summary: A dedicated sysctl policy sets accept_redirects and accept_source_route to 0 for all, default, eth0, and loopback. All corresponding runtime values were 0 before restart and remained 0 after a confirmed reboot, with the policy file and checksum unchanged.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use an implementation compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The system remained RHEL 7.9 with kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64 before and after execution. The implementation used the platform's native sysctl mechanism and did not install or replace software.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Direct runtime and post-reboot observations establish persistent IPv4 hardening, and the OS release and kernel were retained. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for node1: healthy pre-restart state and boot identity, restart acknowledgement and bounded unavailability, a different post-restart identity, and recovered system, SSH, networking, filesystem, policy, and failed-unit state were captured. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the reboot.
limitations: Package-manager consistency collection timed out both before and after execution, so package health was not independently verified; no package-changing command was observed.
The fixed lifecycle snapshots do not collect sysctl values, so the hardened state is established by executor command evidence rather than an independent lifecycle probe.

operational_hygiene.summary: Every observed state-changing command had a clear role: cmd-4da95f2b3cec4da6 created and applied the required hardening policy, while cmd-61a2a1592d3246a3 performed the mandatory restart protocol and validated persistence. No unnecessary mutations were identified. The changed boot-scoped temporary directories and socket process IDs are normal reboot effects; no failed services, new listeners, abandoned files, or unsafe exposure were observed.
